{{short description|Human experimentation that violates ethical principles}}
'''Unethical human experimentation''' is [[human experimentation]] that violates the principles of [[medical ethics]]. Such practices have included denying patients the right to [[informed consent]], using [[pseudoscientific]] frameworks such as [[race science]], and [[medical torture|torturing]] people under the guise of research. Around [[World War II]], [[Japanese war crimes#Human experimentation and biological warfare|Imperial Japan]] and [[Nazi human experimentation|Nazi Germany]] carried out brutal experiments on prisoners and civilians through groups like [[Unit 731]] or individuals like [[Josef Mengele]]; the [[Nuremberg Code]] was developed after the war in response to the Nazi experiments. Countries have carried out brutal experiments on marginalized populations. Examples include [[Unethical human experimentation in the United States|American abuses]] during [[Project MKUltra]] and the [[Tuskegee syphilis experiments]], and the mistreatment of indigenous populations in Canada and Australia. The [[Declaration of Helsinki]], developed by the [[World Medical Association]], is widely regarded as the cornerstone document on human [[research ethics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.wma.net/e/press/2000_8.htm|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20060927052340/http://www.wma.net/e/press/2000_8.htm|url-status=dead|title=WMA Press Release: WMA revises the Declaration of Helsinki. 9 October 2000|archivedate=September 27, 2006}}</ref><ref name="Bošnjak">{{cite journal |first1=Bošnjak |last1=Snežana |year=2001 |title=The declaration of Helsinki: The cornerstone of research ethics |journal=Archive of Oncology |volume=9 |issue=3 |pages=179–84 |url=http://scindeks.ceon.rs/article.aspx?artid=0354-73100103179B&lang=en |archive-date=2013-12-12 |access-date=2015-07-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131212110542/http://scindeks.ceon.rs/article.aspx?artid=0354-73100103179B |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Tyebkhan 2003">{{cite journal |last1=Tyebkhan |first1=G |title=Declaration of Helsinki: the ethical cornerstone of human clinical research |journal=Indian Journal of Dermatology, Venereology and Leprology |volume=69 |issue=3 |pages=245–7 |year=2003 |pmid=17642902}}</ref>

==Nazi Germany==
{{main|Nazi human experimentation|Doctors' Trial}}
Nazi Germany performed human experimentation on large numbers of prisoners (including children), largely [[Jews]] from across Europe, but also [[Romani people|Romani]], [[Sinti]], [[Polish people|ethnic Poles]], [[Nazi crimes against Soviet POWs|Soviet prisoners of war]], homosexuals and disabled Germans, in its [[Nazi concentration camps|concentration camps]] mainly in the early 1940s, during [[World War II]] and [[the Holocaust]]. Prisoners were [[coercion|forced]] into participating; they did not willingly volunteer and no [[informed consent|consent]] was given for the procedures. Typically, the experiments resulted in [[death]], [[Trauma (medicine)|trauma]], [[illness]], shortening of life, [[disfigurement]], or permanent [[disability]], and as such are considered as examples of [[medical torture]] since the participants had to endure mass amounts of pain.

At [[Auschwitz concentration camp|Auschwitz]] and other German camps, under the direction of [[Eduard Wirths]], selected inmates were subjected to various hazardous experiments that were designed to help German military personnel in combat situations, develop new weapons, aid in the recovery of military personnel who had been injured, and to advance the racial ideology backed by the Third Reich.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/article.php?lang=en&ModuleId=10005168 |title=Nazi Medical Experimentation |access-date=23 March 2008 |work=US Holocaust Memorial Museum |archive-date=31 May 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090531100746/http://www.ushmm.org/wlc/article.php?lang=en |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Aribert Heim]] conducted similar medical experiments at [[Mauthausen-Gusen concentration camp|Mauthausen]]. At Buchenwald, [[Carl Værnet]] conducted experiments on homosexual prisoners in an attempt to "cure" homosexuality.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |vauthors=Kondziella D, Hansen K, Zeidman L |date=2013 |title=Scandinavian Neuroscience during the Nazi Era |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/ACBC220A8078D949E217E066C4A45A82/S0317167100014578a.pdf/scandinavian_neuroscience_during_the_nazi_era.pdf |journal=Canadian Journal of Neurological Sciences |volume=40 |issue=4 |pages=493–502 |doi=10.1017/S0317167100014578 |pmid=23786731 |archive-date=2024-06-24 |access-date=2023-10-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240624052135/https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/ACBC220A8078D949E217E066C4A45A82/S0317167100014578a.pdf/scandinavian_neuroscience_during_the_nazi_era.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>

After the war, these crimes were tried at what became known as the [[Doctors' Trial]], and the abuses perpetrated led to the development of the [[Nuremberg Code]] of [[medical ethics]].<ref name="Angel of Death: Josef Mengele">{{cite web|title=Angel of Death: Josef Mengele|url=http://auschwitz.dk/Mengele.htm|publisher=Auschwitz website|access-date=11 March 2013|archive-date=20 January 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130120123527/http://www.auschwitz.dk/Mengele.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> During the Nuremberg Trials, 23 Nazi doctors and scientists were tried for the unethical treatment of concentration camp inmates, who were often used as research subjects with fatal consequences. Of those 23, 16 were convicted (15 were convicted for the unethical treatment, while one of them was only convicted of SS membership), 7 were condemned to death, 9 received prison sentences from 10 years to life, and 7 were acquitted.<ref>{{cite book | last= Mitscherlich | first = A |author2=Mielke F | chapter = Epilogue: Seven Were Hanged|editor1= Annas GJ |editor2=Grodin MA | title = The Nazi Doctors And The Nuremberg Code - Human Rights in Human Experimentation | location = New York | publisher = [[Oxford University Press]] | year = 1992 | pages = [https://books.google.com/books?id=4P04DuPIfAYC&pg=PA105 105–107]}}</ref>

===Before World War II===
The [[Law for the Prevention of Genetically Defective Progeny]], passed on 14 July 1933, legalized the involuntary sterilization of persons with diseases claimed to be hereditary: weak-mindedness, schizophrenia, alcohol abuse, insanity, blindness, deafness, and physical deformities. The law was used to encourage growth of the Aryan race through the sterilization of persons who fell under the quota of being genetically defective.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gardella | first1 = JE | year = 1999 | title = The cost-effectiveness of killing: an overview of Nazi "euthanasia | journal = Medical Sentinel | volume = 4 | pages = 132–5 }}</ref> 1% of citizens between the age of 17 to 24 had been sterilized within two years of the law passing. Within four years, 300,000 patients had been sterilized.<ref>Dahl M. [Selection and destruction-treatment of "unworthy-to-live" children in the Third Reich and the role of child and adolescent psychiatry], Prax Kinderpsychol Kinderpsychiatr 2001;50:170-91.</ref> From about March 1941 to about January 1945, [[Forced sterilization|sterilization]] experiments were conducted at Auschwitz, Ravensbrück, and other places by [[Carl Clauberg]].<ref name="trials">{{cite web |title=Introduction to NMT Case 1: U.S.A. v. Karl Brandt et al. |work=Harvard Law Library, Nuremberg Trials Project: A Digital Document Collection |url=http://nuremberg.law.harvard.edu/php/docs_swi.php?DI=1&text=medical |access-date=23 March 2008 |archive-date=20 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820110259/http://nuremberg.law.harvard.edu/php/docs_swi.php?DI=1&text=medical |url-status=live }}</ref> The purpose of these experiments was to develop a method of sterilization which would be suitable for sterilizing millions of people with a minimum of time and effort. These experiments were conducted by means of [[X-ray]], surgery and various [[medication|drugs]]. Thousands of victims were sterilized. Aside from its experimentation, the Nazi government sterilized around 400,000 people as part of its [[compulsory sterilization]] program.<ref>{{cite web |author=Piotrowski, Christa |title=Dark Chapter of American History: U.S. Court Battle Over Forced Sterilization |date=21 July 2000 |work=CommonDreams.org News Center |url=http://www.commondreams.org/views/072100-106.htm |access-date=23 March 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080415181618/http://www.commondreams.org/views/072100-106.htm |archive-date=15 April 2008 }}</ref> Intravenous injections of solutions speculated to contain [[iodine]] and [[silver nitrate]] were successful, but had unwanted side effects, such as vaginal bleeding, severe abdominal pain, and cervical cancer.<ref>{{cite news |author=Meric, Vesna |title=Forced to take part in experiments |date=27 January 2005 |work=BBC News |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/4212061.stm |archive-date=26 November 2024 |access-date=13 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241126222149/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/4212061.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Therefore, [[gamma radiation|radiation]] treatment became the favored choice of sterilization. Specific amounts of exposure to radiation destroyed a person's ability to produce ova or sperm. The radiation was administered through deception. Prisoners were brought into a room and asked to complete forms, which took two to three minutes. In this time, the radiation treatment was administered and, unknown to the prisoners, they were rendered completely sterile. Many suffered severe [[radiation burns]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Medical Experiments at Auschwitz |work=Jewish Virtual Library |url=https://www.jewishvirtuallibrary.org/jsource/Holocaust/aumed.html |access-date=23 March 2008 |archive-date=12 January 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170112141643/http://www.jewishvirtuallibrary.org/jsource/Holocaust/aumed.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Eugen Fischer]] began sterilization experimentation in German-occupied [[South West Africa]] during World War I. <!--Expand - when was this done and what was being studied? This is very indirect--> A supporter of forced sterilization as a means to prevent the growth of inferior populations and a member of the Nazi Party, Fischer focused his experimentation on [[mixed-race]] children in order to justify the Nazi Party's ban on [[interracial marriage]]. As a result of Fischer's research in Namibia, Germany prohibited marriages between people of different races in its colonies.<ref>Friedlander, Henry. 1997. ''The Origins of Nazi Genocide: From Euthanasia to the Final Solution'', University of North Carolina Press</ref>

===During World War II===
[[File:Child survivors of Auschwitz.jpeg|thumb|Jewish twins were kept alive to be used in [[Josef Mengele]]'s medical experiments. These children from [[Auschwitz concentration camp|Auschwitz]] were liberated by the Red Army in January 1945.]]
The ''[[Luftwaffe]]'' performed a series of 360 to 400 experiments at [[Dachau concentration camp|Dachau]] and [[Auschwitz]], in which [[hypothermia]] was induced in 280 to 300 victims.<ref name=Bogod>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1111/j.1365-2044.2004.04034.x|pmid = 15549970|title = The Nazi Hypothermia Experiments: Forbidden Data?|journal = Anaesthesia|volume = 59|issue = 12|pages = 1155–1156|year = 2004|last1 = Bogod|first1 = David|doi-access = }}</ref><ref name="BERGER" /> These were conducted for the [[Nazi]] high command to simulate the conditions the armies suffered on the [[Eastern Front (World War II)|Eastern Front]], as the German forces were ill-prepared for the cold weather they encountered. Many experiments were conducted on captured Russian troops; the Nazis wondered whether their genetics gave them superior resistance to cold.<ref name="NOVA">{{cite web |author=Tyson, Peter |title=Holocaust on Trial: The Experiments |work=NOVA Online |url=https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/nova/holocaust/experiside.html |access-date=23 March 2008 |archive-date=4 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170904154933/http://www.pbs.org/wgbh/nova/holocaust/experiside.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Approximately 100 people are reported to have died as a result of these experiments.<ref>Neurnberg Military Tribunal, Volume I · [http://www.mazal.org/archive/nmt/01/NMT01-T200.htm Page 200] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160603194801/http://www.mazal.org/archive/nmt/01/NMT01-T200.htm |date=2016-06-03 }}</ref>

In early 1942, prisoners at Dachau concentration camp were used by Sigmund Rascher in experiments to aid German pilots who had to [[ejection seat|eject]] at high altitudes. A [[pressure vessel|low-pressure chamber]] containing these prisoners was used to simulate conditions at altitudes of up to 20,000&nbsp;m (66,000&nbsp;ft).<ref name=Cockburn>{{cite book |last=Cockburn |first=Alexander |title=Whiteout:The CIA, Drugs, and the Press |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=s5qIj_h_PtkC&q=%22sigmund+rascher%22+brain&pg=PA149 |year=1998 |publisher=Verso |isbn=1-85984-139-2 }}</ref> Of the 200 subjects, 80 died outright, and the others were executed.<ref name="NOVA"/>

Other experiments included:an experiment in repeated head injury which drove a boy insane,<ref name=Small>Small, Martin; Vic Shayne. [https://books.google.com/books?id=kaIYMRYufh0C&dq=%22Dr.+wichtmann%22&pg=PA135 "Remember Us: My Journey from the Shtetl through the Holocaust"], Page 135, 2009.</ref> experiments at [[Buchenwald concentration camp|Buchenwald]] where poisons were secretly administered in food,<ref name="trials"/> experiments to test the effect of various pharmaceutical preparations on [[phosphorus]] burns induced with material from [[incendiary bomb]]s,<ref name="trials"/> experiments at Ravensbrück to investigate the effectiveness of [[sulfonamide (medicine)|sulfonamide]] after infection with [[bacterium|bacteria]] such as ''[[Clostridium perfringens]]'' (the causative agent in [[gas gangrene]]) and ''[[Clostridium tetani]]'' (the causative agent in [[tetanus]]),<ref name="Schaefer">Schaefer, Naomi. ''[http://www.thenewatlantis.com/archive/5/schaefer.htm The Legacy of Nazi Medicine] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080907072046/http://www.thenewatlantis.com/archive/5/schaefer.htm |date=2008-09-07 }}'', ''The New Atlantis'', Number 5, Spring 2004, pp. 54–60.</ref><ref name=Spitz>{{cite book |last=Spitz |first=Vivien |title=Doctors from Hell: The Horrific Account of Nazi Experiments on Humans |url=https://archive.org/details/doctorsfromhellh00spit |url-access=registration |page=[https://archive.org/details/doctorsfromhellh00spit/page/4 4] |quote=sulfonamide nazi tetanus. |year=2005 |publisher=Sentient Publications |isbn=1-59181-032-9 }}</ref> experiments conducted to attempt treatments of [[chemical burns]] induced by [[sulfur mustard|mustard gas]] and similar compounds,<ref name="trials"/> and experiments at Dachau to study various methods of making [[sea water]] drinkable.<ref name="NOVA"/><ref name="ETHIC">{{cite web |author=Cohen, Baruch C. |title=The Ethics Of Using Medical Data From Nazi Experiments |work=Jewish Law: Articles |url=http://www.jlaw.com/Articles/NaziMedEx.html |access-date=23 March 2008 |archive-date=13 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160313125644/http://www.jlaw.com/Articles/NaziMedEx.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Many of the subjects died as a result of the experiments, while many others were executed after the tests were completed to study the effect [[post-mortem examination|post mortem]].<ref name="CHILD">{{cite web |author=Rosenberg, Jennifer |title=Mengele's Children – The Twins of Auschwitz |work=about.com |url=http://history1900s.about.com/od/auschwitz/a/mengeletwins.htm |access-date=23 March 2008 |archive-date=19 February 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170219040801/http://history1900s.about.com/od/auschwitz/a/mengeletwins.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> Those who survived were often left mutilated, which resulted in permanent disability, weakened bodies, and mental distress.<ref name="NOVA"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Sterilization Experiments |work=Jewish Virtual Library |url=https://www.jewishvirtuallibrary.org/jsource/Holocaust/sterilexp.html |access-date=23 March 2008 |archive-date=9 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161209042527/http://www.jewishvirtuallibrary.org/jsource/Holocaust/sterilexp.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

The results of the Dachau freezing experiments have been used in some modern research into the treatment of hypothermia, with at least 45 publications having referenced the experiments since the [[Second World War]].<ref name="BERGER">{{cite journal |title=Nazi Science — The Dachau Hypothermia Experiments |author=Robert L. Berger, M.D. |year=1990 |journal=The New England Journal of Medicine |volume=322 |issue=20|pages=1435–1440 |doi=10.1056/NEJM199005173222006 |pmid=2184357|doi-access=free }}</ref> This, together with the recent use of data from Nazi research into the effects of [[phosgene]] gas, has proven controversial and presents an [[medical ethics|ethical]] dilemma for modern physicians who do not agree with the methods used to obtain this data.<ref name="ETHIC"/> Some object on an ethical basis, and others have rejected Nazi research purely on scientific grounds, pointing out methodological inconsistencies. In an often-cited review of the Dachau hypothermia experiments, Berger states that the study has "all the ingredients of a scientific fraud" and that the data "cannot advance science or save human lives."<ref name="BERGER"/>

Several Nazi experimenters were after the war employed by the United States government in [[Operation Paperclip]] and later similar efforts.{{Citation needed|date=March 2022}}

==Japan==
===Empire of Japan===
[[File:Unit 731 - Complex.jpg|thumb|Japanese Unit 731 Complex that used humans for experimentation for biological and chemical weapons, as well as live vivisections and other experiments]]
Human subject research in Japan began in World War II. It continued for some years after. [[Unit 731]], a department of the [[Imperial Japanese Army]] located near [[Harbin]] (then in the puppet state of [[Manchukuo]], in northeast China), experimented on prisoners by conducting [[vivisection]]s, dismemberments, and bacterial inoculations. It induced epidemics on a very large scale from 1932 onward through the [[Second Sino-Japanese War]].<ref name="gold"/> It also conducted biological and chemical weapons tests on prisoners and captured POWs. With the expansion of the empire during [[World War II]], similar units were set up in conquered cities such as [[Nanjing]] ([[Unit 1644]]), [[Beijing]] ([[Unit 1855]]), [[Guangzhou]] ([[Unit 8604]]) and [[Singapore]] ([[Unit 9420]]). After the war, Supreme Commander of the Occupation [[Douglas MacArthur]] gave immunity in the name of the [[United States]] to [[Shirō Ishii]] and all members of the units in exchange for all of the results of their experiments.<ref name="gold">{{cite book | last = Gold | first = H | isbn = 0-8048-3565-9 | title = Unit 731 Testimony | year = 2003 | pages = [https://books.google.com/books?id=cprBEpxvexgC&pg=PA109 109] | publisher = [[Tuttle Publishing]] | edition = 5}}</ref> The United States blocked [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] access to this information. The Soviets prosecuted some of the Unit 731 members during its [[Khabarovsk War Crime Trials]].

In November 2006, Doctor [[Akira Makino]] confessed to Kyodo news that he had performed surgery and amputations on condemned prisoners, including women and children, in 1944 and 1945 while he was stationed on [[Mindanao]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Japanese doctor admits POW abuse |publisher=[[BBC News]] |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/6185442.stm |date=26 November 2006 |archive-date=26 August 2025 |access-date=13 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250826222132/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/6185442.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Most of Makino's victims were [[Moro people|Moro Muslims]].<ref>{{cite news |title=A life haunted by WWII surgical killings |date=October 31, 2007 |work=bt.com.bn |url=http://www.bt.com.bn/focus/2007/10/31/a_life_haunted_by_wwii_surgical_killings |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141213021214/http://www.bt.com.bn/focus/2007/10/31/a_life_haunted_by_wwii_surgical_killings |archive-date=December 13, 2014 |url-status=usurped}}</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20140317024425/http://www.google.com/hostednews/afp/article/ALeqM5ht5P8U54dLa7dH9mqjKyurq0zQMw?hl=en AFP ''Japanese veteran haunted by WWII surgical killings'' 2007.]</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/editorials/archives/2007/11/06/2003386494|title=Japanese war veteran speaks of atrocities in the Philippines - Taipei Times|date=November 6, 2007|website=www.taipeitimes.com|access-date=September 18, 2024|archive-date=February 17, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220217095028/http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/editorials/archives/2007/11/06/2003386494|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.theaustralian.com.au/news/world/dissect-them-alive-chilling-imperial-that-order-could-not-be-di/story-e6frg6so-1111113061584|title=Parry, "The Australian" ''Dissect them alive: chilling Imperial that order could not be disobeyed'' 2007.|access-date=2015-07-04|archive-date=2015-02-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150214145048/http://www.theaustralian.com.au/news/world/dissect-them-alive-chilling-imperial-that-order-could-not-be-di/story-e6frg6so-1111113061584|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/news/world/asia/article2606909.ece|title=Parry, "The Times" ''Dissect them alive: order not to be disobeyed'' 2007.|website=[[The Times]]|access-date=2015-07-04|archive-date=2007-02-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070228095300/http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/news/world/asia/article1438491.ece|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2007, Doctor [[Ken Yuasa]] testified to ''[[The Japan Times]]'' and said that he believes that at least 1,000 persons working for the [[Shōwa period|Shōwa]] regime, including surgeons, conducted surgical research in mainland China.<ref>{{cite news |last=Hongo |first=Jun |quote=I was afraid during my first vivisection, but the second time around, it was much easier. By the third time, I was willing to do it. |title=Vivisectionnist recalls his day of reckoning |publisher=[[The Japan Times]] |url=http://search.japantimes.co.jp/cgi-bin/nn20071024w1.html}}</ref>

===State of Japan===
In incidents throughout the 1950s, former Unit 731 members infected prisoners and mental health patients with deadly diseases.<ref>{{cite book | title = ''日本弁護士連合会『人権白書昭和43年版』日本弁護士連合会、''| year = 1968 | pages = 126–136}}</ref> In 1958, a large number of infants were brought to Kobe Medical School and forcibly administered sugar by having needles inserted through their noses and into their stomachs. A tube was inserted into their anuses to determine how the sugar was processed by their digestive systems. Many of the infants experienced diarrhea and anal bleeding. The parents were never informed that their children were being used as test subjects.<ref>
清水昭美『増補・生体実験』三一新書、1979年；日比逸郎「臨床研究と生体実験」『ジュリスト臨時増刊・医療と人権』(No.548)、有斐閣、1973年11月、pp.18-23</ref>

The US army and Japanese government they installed refused to help Japanese atomic bomb victims (Hibakusha) and instead collected data on them and took samples of their organs after they died.<ref>{{cite journal |first=Shingo |date=1996 |title=the atomic victims as human guinea pigs |url=https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/527435-atomic-bomb-victims.html |last=Shibata |journal=Seisen Review |number=4 |archive-date=2024-02-23 |access-date=2024-02-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240223083602/https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/527435-atomic-bomb-victims.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130210011533/http://docs8.chomikuj.pl/2097817100%2CPL%2C0%2C0%2CHiroshima---Atomic-Victims-as-Human-Guinea-Pigs-%28criminal-Japan%E2%80%99s-National-Institute-of-Health-%28JNIH%29-Prof.-Shingo-Shibata-1996%29.pdf | url=http://docs8.chomikuj.pl/2097817100%2CPL%2C0%2C0%2CHiroshima---Atomic-Victims-as-Human-Guinea-Pigs-%28criminal-Japan%E2%80%99s-National-Institute-of-Health-%28JNIH%29-Prof.-Shingo-Shibata-1996%29.pdf | archive-date=2013-02-10 | title=The tomic Victims as Human Pigs | access-date=2024-02-23 | url-status=dead }}</ref> The US military paid Japanese members of Unit 731 to conduct experiments on Japanese people in Japan in 1952, with a Japanese girl dying after multiple Japanese babies were deliberately infected with [[Escherichia coli|E. coli]] bacteria at Nagoya City University Hospital by Jiro Ogawa. Japanese patients at a mental hospital were infected with scrub typhus in 1953–1956 with one of them killing himself to escape the torture and another 9 Japanese patients died of the typhus itself.<ref>{{cite news |last=McGill |first=Peter |date=Aug 21, 1983 |title=Postwar Japan: "US Backed Japan's Germ Tests on Mentally Sick" |page=6 |work=The Observer |location=London, Greater London, England |url=
https://theguardian.newspapers.com/article/the-observer-postwar-japan-us-backed-j/122763034/}}</ref>

== Indigenous Australians ==
In the 1920s and 1930s, [[Aboriginal Australians]] and [[Torres Strait Islanders]] were subject to medical experiments on how they experienced pain and where body measurements and blood samples were forcibly taken. The experiments were motivated by a system of [[scientific racism]] and were carried out by researchers from the [[University of Adelaide]]. In 2002, the vice chancellor of the university described the experiments as "degrading and in some cases barbarous" and the school issued a formal apology to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander groups.<ref>{{cite journal | title = The Cultivation of Whiteness: Science, Health and Racial Destiny in Australia (book review) |journal = BMJ: British Medical Journal| author = Joff Lelliott | publisher = British Medical Journal | year = 2003 | volume = 326 | number = 7394 | page = 888|pmc = 1125797|doi = 10.1136/bmj.326.7394.888}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.adelaide.edu.au/news/news314.html | title = Apology for Past Experiments on Aboriginal People | date = 2002-02-08 |website=University of Adelaide | access-date = 2018-08-04}}</ref>

== Indigenous populations in Canada ==
{{see also|Canadian Indian residential school system}}
Canada has historically carried out unethical medical experiments on indigenous populations in concert with its policies of forced [[cultural assimilation]]. In 1933, about 600 Native children from the reserves near [[Qu'Appelle, Saskatchewan]], were enrolled in a trial to test the [[BCG vaccine|tuberculosis vaccine]]. During the course of the trial, in both the control and treatment groups nearly a fifth "died from diseases of poverty, gastroenteritis and pneumonia, as a result of the lethal living conditions on the reserves." Parental consent was not sought for indigenous children, though it was sought for the non-indigenous.<ref>{{cite journal | author = Lux, M. | year = 1998 | title = Perfect subjects: race, tuberculosis, and the Qu'Appelle BCG Vaccine Trial | journal = Canadian Bulletin of Medical History | volume = 15 | number = 2 | pages = 277–295| doi = 10.3138/cbmh.15.2.277 | pmid = 11624067 | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref>{{cite news | author = Leslie Young | title = What happened to Jim? Experiments on Canada's indigenous populations | url = https://globalnews.ca/news/2503875/what-happened-to-jim-experiments-on-canadas-indigenous-populations/ | publisher = Global News | date = 2016-02-08 | access-date = 2018-08-04}}</ref>
Between 1942 and 1952, malnourished children from six residential schools were used in experiments without consent or parental notification. They were split into [[treatment and control groups]] and denied increases in nutrition, despite the researchers believing malnutrition to be a serious problem in the schools, as they were used to determine whether certain combinations of supplements mitigated problems. Children died, developed [[anemia]], and were in some cases denied dental care previously available to them as they developed [[tooth decay|cavities]] and [[gingivitis]]. The experiments were run by the [[Crown–Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada|Department of Indian Affairs of Canada]] and directed by Percy Moore and [[Frederick Tisdall]], a former president of the [[Canadian Paediatric Society]].<ref>{{cite journal | title = Canada's shameful history of nutrition research on residential school children: the need for strong medical ethics in Aboriginal health research |journal = Paediatrics & Child Health|volume = 19|issue = 2| author = Noni E MacDonald | date = 2014 | publisher = Oxford University Press | page = 64|pmc = 3941673|pmid = 24596474|doi = 10.1093/pch/19.2.64}}</ref> In 2014, the Society released a statement outlining guidelines for community-based participatory research involving [[Inuit]], [[Métis]], and [[First Nations in Canada|First Nations]] youth.<ref>{{cite journal | author = Lola T. Baydala and Jill M. Starkes | title = Health research involving First Nations, Inuit and Métis children and their communities. | journal = Paediatrics & Child Health | volume = 19 | pages = 99–102 | number = 2 | year = 2014 |pmc = 3941676| pmid = 24596485 | doi = 10.1093/pch/19.2.99 }}</ref>

== Canada (General) ==
From 1957 to 1964, a series of [[Central Intelligence Agency|CIA]]-funded unethical medical experiments known as the [[Montreal experiments]], or MKUltra Subproject 69, were carried out in Montreal by Scottish psychiatrist [[Donald Ewen Cameron]] at [[McGill University]]'s [[Allan Memorial Institute]]. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Montreal MKULTRA Experiments |url=https://thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/mkultra |access-date=2026-02-19 |website=thecanadianencyclopedia.ca |language=en |archive-date=2025-09-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250925014636/https://www.thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/mkultra |url-status=live }}</ref> While the official purpose of these experiments was to "cure" [[schizophrenia]] by reprogramming patients' memories, it is suspected they were actually attempts to master mind control. Patients, who were often admitted into the hospital in vulnerable conditions, were not informed that they were being used for experimental research. They were subjected to abusive techniques such as intensive [[electroconvulsive therapy]], [[sensory deprivation]], drug-induced comas, and repeated audio messages that resulted in memory loss and long-term psychological impacts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=North |first=Harry |date=31 July 2025 |title=Survivors of CIA-linked mind-control tests in Montreal win right to sue McGill, Ottawa |url=https://montrealgazette.com/news/survivors-of-cia-linked-mind-control-tests-in-montreal-win-right-to-sue-mcgill-ottawa |access-date=19 February 2026 |website=Montreal Gazette}}</ref> In addition, a case was brought forward in 2023 by the Mohawk Mothers against McGill University asserting the presence of [[Unmarked grave|unmarked graves]] following these experiments on the site of the Institute, which McGill is contesting.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Mulowayi-Pelletier |first=Tatiana |date=2024-06-11 |title=Excavation à l’ancien hôpital Royal Victoria: « Nous parlons de personnes vivantes qui sont décédées » |url=https://www.lapresse.ca/actualites/justice-et-faits-divers/2024-06-11/excavation-a-l-ancien-hopital-royal-victoria/nous-parlons-de-personnes-vivantes-qui-sont-decedees.php |access-date=2026-02-19 |work=La Presse |language=fr-CA |archive-date=2024-08-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240829140451/https://www.lapresse.ca/actualites/justice-et-faits-divers/2024-06-11/excavation-a-l-ancien-hopital-royal-victoria/nous-parlons-de-personnes-vivantes-qui-sont-decedees.php |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bordeleau |first=Jean-Louis |last2=L'Homme |first2=Charles-Olivier |date=29 June 2023 |title=De possibles tombes autochtones découvertes près de l’Université McGill |url=https://www.ledevoir.com/actualites/societe/793868/des-tombes-autochtones-potentiellement-decouvertes-pres-de-mcgill |access-date=19 February 2026 |website=Le Devoir}}</ref> They claim that these graves belong to both Indigenous and non-Indigenous patients.<ref name=":0" />

==Guatemala==
{{main|Syphilis experiments in Guatemala}}

From 1946 to 1948 U.S. scientific researchers in Guatemala infected hundreds of mental patients with [[sexually transmitted diseases]] (STD). Researchers from the U.S. Public Health Service (PHS) conducted experiments on approximately 1,500 male and female patients housed at Guatemala's National Mental Health Hospital.<ref name=CDCFactScheet>{{cite web | url = https://www.hhs.gov/1946inoculationstudy/factsheet.html | title = Fact Sheet on the 1946-1948 U.S. Public Health Service Sexually Transmitted Diseases (STD) Inoculation Study | publisher = [[United States Department of Health and Human Services]] | access-date = 2013-04-15 | date = n.d. | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130425164618/http://www.hhs.gov/1946inoculationstudy/factsheet.html | archive-date = 2013-04-25 }}</ref> The scientists injected the patients with gonorrhea and syphilis—and encouraged many of them to pass the disease on to others. The experiments were done in cooperation with the Guatemalan government. The PHS carried out the experiments under the guise of syphilis inoculations. In 2010 these experiments were revealed by Susan Reverby of [[Wellesley College]], who was researching a book on the [[Tuskegee syphilis experiment]]s. The US [[United States Secretary of State|Secretary of State]] [[Hillary Clinton]] issued an official apology to Guatemala.<ref name="nyt20101001">{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/10/02/health/research/02infect.html?_r=0 |title=U.S. Apologizes for Syphilis Experiment |date=1 October 2010 |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=2 October 2010}}</ref> President [[Barack Obama]] apologized to President [[Álvaro Colom]], who had called these experiments "a [[crimes against humanity|crime against humanity]]".<ref name="BBC20101001">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-11457552 |title=US medical tests in Guatemala 'crime against humanity' |date=1 October 2010 |publisher=BBC News |access-date=2 October 2010 |archive-date=2 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160102060840/http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-11457552 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==North Korea==
{{main|Human experimentation in North Korea}}

==Sweden==
The [[Vipeholm experiments]] were a series of human experiments where patients of Vipeholm Hospital for intellectually disabled in [[Lund]], Sweden, were fed large amounts of sweets to provoke [[dental caries]] between 1945 and 1955. The experiments were sponsored both by the sugar industry and dentist community, in an effort to determine whether [[carbohydrates]] affected the formation of cavities. The experiments provided extensive knowledge about [[dental health]] and resulted in enough empirical data to link the intake of sugar to dental caries.<ref>{{cite journal |pmid=13196991 |year=1954 |last1=Gustafsson |first1=BE |last2=Quensel |first2=CE |last3=Lanke |first3=LS |last4=Lundqvist |first4=C |last5=Grahnen |first5=H |last6=Bonow |first6=BE |last7=Krasse |first7=B |title=The Vipeholm dental caries study; the effect of different levels of carbohydrate intake on caries activity in 436 individuals observed for five years |volume=11 |issue=3–4 |pages=232–64 |journal=Acta Odontologica Scandinavica |doi=10.3109/00016355308993925|doi-access=free }}</ref> However, today they are considered to have violated the principles of [[medical ethics]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Krasse |first=Bo |date=September 2001 |title=The Vipeholm Dental Caries Study: Recollections and Reflections 50 Years Later |journal=Journal of Dental Research |volume=80 |issue=9 |pages=1785–1788 |doi=10.1177/00220345010800090201 |pmid=11926233 |issn=0022-0345}}</ref>

==Soviet Union==
{{Main|Poison laboratory of the Soviet secret services}}

The [[Soviet Union]] manufactured and tested poisons in the poison laboratory of the Soviet secret services, variously known as Special Office, Laboratory 1, Laboratory 12, Central Investigation Institute for Special Technology and Kamera ({{langx|ru|Камера}}).<ref>[http://www.svobodanews.ru/content/transcript/1747128.html KGB Poison Factory: From Lenin to Litvinenko] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120218110821/http://www.svobodanews.ru/content/transcript/1747128.html |date=February 18, 2012 }}, [[RFE/RL]], interview with Boris Volodarsky (Russian) - [https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB111282082770699984 English version] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170818010635/https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB111282082770699984 |date=August 18, 2017 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=Shoham, D. |author2=Wolfson, Z. | title = The Russian Biological Weapons Program: Vanished or Disappeared? | journal = Critical Reviews in Microbiology | volume = 30 | issue = 4 |date= October–December 2004 | pages = 241–261 | doi = 10.1080/10408410490468812 | pmid= 15646399|s2cid= 30487628 }}</ref> The laboratory was reportedly reactivated by the Russian government in the late 1990s.<ref name="Harding">{{Cite book|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2016/mar/06/alexander-litvinenko-and-the-most-radioactive-towel-in-history|title=Alexander Litvinenko and the most radioactive towel in history|last=Harding|first=Luke|date=2016-03-06|newspaper=The Guardian|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077|access-date=2016-03-12|archive-date=August 19, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230819194541/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2016/mar/06/alexander-litvinenko-and-the-most-radioactive-towel-in-history|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/08/21/world/europe/moscow-kremlin-silence-critics-poison.html|title=More of Kremlin's Opponents Are Ending Up Dead|last=Kramer|first=Andrew E.|date=2016-08-20|newspaper=The New York Times|issn=0362-4331|access-date=2016-08-21|archive-date=August 21, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160821014408/http://www.nytimes.com/2016/08/21/world/europe/moscow-kremlin-silence-critics-poison.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Grigory Mairanovsky]], head of Laboratory 1, and his colleagues tested a variety of lethal poisons on prisoners from the [[Gulag]]s, including [[mustard gas]], [[ricin]], [[digitoxin]], [[curare]], cyanide, and many others.<ref name="Meier">Andrew Meier. 2008. ''The Lost Spy: An American in Stalin's Secret Service'', W. W. Norton.</ref> The objective of these experiments was to identify a tasteless, odorless chemical that could not be detected {{lang|la|[[post mortem]]}}. Candidate poisons were administered to the victims along with a meal or drink, disguised as "medication".<ref name="Birstein">Vadim J. Birstein. ''The Perversion Of Knowledge: The True Story of Soviet Science.'' Westview Press (2004) {{ISBN|0-8133-4280-5}}.</ref> Mairanovsky intentionally brought individuals of various physical conditions and ages into the laboratory to comprehensively understand the effects of each poison.

[[Pavel Sudoplatov]] and [[Nahum Eitingon]] approved specialized equipment (namely, poisons) only if it had been tested on "humans", as revealed in the [[Mitrokhin Archive|testimony of Mikhail Filimonov]].<ref name="Birstein"/> [[Vsevolod Nikolayevich Merkulov|Vsevolod Merkulov]] stated that these experiments received authorization from NKVD chief [[Lavrentiy Beria]].<ref name="Birstein"/> Following Stalin's death and Beria's subsequent arrest, Beria attested on August 28, 1953, that "I gave orders to Mairanovsky to conduct experiments on people sentenced to the highest measure of punishment, but it was not my idea".<ref name="Birstein"/>

==United Kingdom==
De-classified documents from [[The National Archives (United Kingdom)|The National Archives]] revealed that during the 20th century, scientists from [[Porton Down]] conducted experiments on British and Indian soldiers to test the effects of [[mustard gas]]. From 1916 until 1989, more than 20,000 British servicemen were subjected to [[chemical warfare]] trials. The experiments on Indian servicemen were conducted in [[Rawalpindi]], [[British Raj|British India]], during the 1930s and 1940s. It is unclear whether the Indian trial subjects, some of whom were hospitalized as a result of their injuries, were all volunteers.<ref>{{cite web |title=Military scientists tested mustard gas on Indians |url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2007/sep/01/india.military |website=The Guardian |date=September 2007 |access-date=13 April 2017 |archive-date=19 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171019220358/https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2007/sep/01/india.military |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url = https://www.voanews.com/english/news/a-13-2007-09-02-voa11.html | title = Report: Britain Tested Chemical Weapons on Indian Colonial Troops | publisher = [[Voice of America]] | date = 2007-09-02 | access-date = 2011-06-02 | url-status = live | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120209033840/http://www.voanews.com/english/news/a-13-2007-09-02-voa11.html | archive-date = 2012-02-09 }}</ref> In the 1950s, [[Royal Air Force]] engineer [[Ronald Maddison]] was killed when he was exposed to 200 milligrams of [[sarin]] at [[Porton Down]]. He had believed that he was testing a cure for the common cold, and in 2004 a High Court judgement ruled that his death was "unlawful".<ref>{{cite web | url =http://www.aerotoxic.org/download/docs/reports_and_evidence/OPReport.pdf | title =Organophosphate Report | work =Aerotoxic Association | date =4 December 2019 }}{{Dead link|date=July 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=no }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Nerve gas death was 'unlawful'|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/wiltshire/4013767.stm|publisher=BBC News|access-date=2013-01-20|date=15 November 2004|archive-date=2012-10-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024074047/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/wiltshire/4013767.stm|url-status=live}}</ref>

Between 1940 and 1979, the [[Ministry of Defence (United Kingdom)|Ministry of Defence]] secretly dispersed potentially dangerous chemicals and micro-organisms across much of the country to evaluate readiness against a biological attack from the Soviet Union. They dropped [[zinc cadmium sulfide|zinc cadmium sulphide]] from aircraft and dispersed it by land to track the spread of fluorescent particles, and also spread ''[[Escherichia coli|E. coli]]'', ''[[Bacillus globigii]]'', and ''[[Serratia marcescens]]'' bacteria.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Barnett |first1=Antony |title=Millions were in germ war tests |url=https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2002/apr/21/uk.medicalscience |website=The Guardian |date=21 April 2002 |publisher=Guardian News & Media Limited |access-date=16 May 2020 |archive-date=20 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200820062147/https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2002/apr/21/uk.medicalscience |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Turkey==
The Depth Research Laboratory (DAL) was the name given to the political branch known as "D Group" within the Ankara Police Department in the period following the September 12 Coup. D Group later became known as DAL, the initials of the Depth Research Laboratory. The branch came to prominence for systematic torture and ill-treatment of detainees following the September 12 Coup.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=16 April 2016 |archive-date=17 April 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160417112508/http://www.milliyet.com.tr/dal-in-belgesi-var-ama-kendisi-yok-/gundem/gundemdetay/27.01.2013/1660832/default.htm |publisher=www.milliyet.com.tr/ |title=DAL’ın belgesi var ama ‘kendisi yok’ |url=http://www.milliyet.com.tr/dal-in-belgesi-var-ama-kendisi-yok-/gundem/gundemdetay/27.01.2013/1660832/default.htm |url-status=live}}<!-- auto-translated from Turkish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=16 April 2016 |archive-date=17 April 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160417112519/http://www.dha.com.tr/12-eylul-idarecilerine-sorusturma_260778.html |publisher=www.dha.com.tr/ |title=12 Eylül idarecilerine soruşturma |url=http://www.dha.com.tr/12-eylul-idarecilerine-sorusturma_260778.html}}<!-- auto-translated from Turkish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=16 April 2016 |archive-date=29 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150929031037/http://bianet.org/bianet/insan-haklari/134306-yazicioglu-iskencecimdi |first=Ayça |last=Söylemez |publisher=bianet.org |title=AYŞE BAKKALCI ANLATIYOR "Yazıcıoğlu İşkencecimdi" |url=http://bianet.org/bianet/insan-haklari/134306-yazicioglu-iskencecimdi}}<!-- auto-translated from Turkish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=16 April 2016 |archive-date=17 April 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160417112513/http://www.hurriyet.com.tr/ozel-timcileri-gozaltina-alan-yazicioglu-genel-mudur-39032277 |publisher=www.hurriyet.com.tr |title=Özel Timcileri gözaltına alan Yazıcıoğlu Genel Müdür |url=http://www.hurriyet.com.tr/ozel-timcileri-gozaltina-alan-yazicioglu-genel-mudur-39032277 |url-status=live}}<!-- auto-translated from Turkish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

[[Muazzez İlmiye Çığ]] was the chair of the board of the HZİ Neuropsychiatry Foundation and chief advisor to the leader of the Homeland Party, which came into the spotlight after allegations of experimenting on political prisoners during the September 12 coup.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=23 November 2024 |archive-date=21 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241121023849/https://medyascope.tv/2024/11/18/muazzez-ilmiye-cigin-12-eylul-karnesi/ |date=18 November 2024 |first=Ankara |language=tr |last=Büro |title=Muazzez İlmiye Çığ'ın 12 Eylül karnesi |url=https://medyascope.tv/2024/11/18/muazzez-ilmiye-cigin-12-eylul-karnesi/ |work=Medyascope}}<!-- auto-translated from Turkish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref>{{cite web |access-date=11 July 2025 |date=17 November 2024 |language=tr |last=Aydınlık |title=Doğu Perinçek, Muazzez İlmiye Çığ'ı yazdı: Dört kitabın manasını öğreten tarihin kızı |url=https://www.aydinlik.com.tr/koseyazisi/dogu-perincek-muazzez-ilmiye-cigi-yazdi-dort-kitabin-manasini-ogreten-tarihin-kizi-495720 |work=Aydınlık |archive-date=23 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250623140312/https://www.aydinlik.com.tr/koseyazisi/dogu-perincek-muazzez-ilmiye-cigi-yazdi-dort-kitabin-manasini-ogreten-tarihin-kizi-495720 |url-status=live }}<!-- auto-translated from Turkish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> The HZİ Neuropsychiatry Foundation takes its name from the initials of Çığ's mother, Hamide, and father, Zekeriya İtil. Numerous allegations have been made against the foundation that it conducted studies in Turkey testing drugs banned for use in the United States on patients and prisoners.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=19 November 2024 |language=tr |title=’Türk teröristleri geri zekalıdır’ diyen araştırmacı!!! |url=https://www.posta.com.tr/yazarlar/oral-calislar/turk-teroristleri-geri-zekalidir-diyen-arastirmaci-2781749 |work=Posta |archive-date=19 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241119042755/https://www.posta.com.tr/yazarlar/oral-calislar/turk-teroristleri-geri-zekalidir-diyen-arastirmaci-2781749 |url-status=live }}<!-- auto-translated from Turkish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref>{{cite web |access-date=19 November 2024 |date=19 November 2024 |language=tr-TR |publisher=Gazete Duvar |title=İbrahim Aydın, HZİ Nöropsikiyatri Vakfı'nı anlattı: '52 iğne vurdular' |url=https://www.gazeteduvar.com.tr/ibrahim-aydin-hzi-noropsikiyatri-vakfini-anlatti-52-igne-vurdular-haber-1736381 |work=İbrahim Aydın |archive-date=19 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241119124345/https://www.gazeteduvar.com.tr/ibrahim-aydin-hzi-noropsikiyatri-vakfini-anlatti-52-igne-vurdular-haber-1736381 |url-status=live }}<!-- auto-translated from Turkish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> Çığ, İtil, their friends, family, and some of the foundation's staff denied the accusations. They claimed that the experiments were conducted with voluntary participation and were intended to profile terrorists under the HZİ Foundation's supervision, with the permission of the September 12 Military Junta.<ref>{{cite news|access-date=29 November 2024 |archive-date=25 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241125234536/https://www.bbc.com/turkce/articles/c99r5403773o |date=21 November 2024 |first=Merve |last=Kara-Kaşka |publisher=BBC |title=HZİ Vakfı: Yetkililer ve dönemin tanıkları 12 Eylül iddialarıyla ilgili neler anlattı? |url=https://www.bbc.com/turkce/articles/c99r5403773o |url-status=live}}<!-- auto-translated from Turkish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

==United States==
{{Main|Unethical human experimentation in the United States}}

<!--SEE CITATIONS IN MAIN ARTICLE ABOVE-->
Since the late 19th century, numerous human experiments were performed in the United States which were later characterized as [[medical ethics|unethical]]. They were often performed illegally, without the knowledge, [[consent]], or [[informed consent]] of the test subjects. Examples have included the deliberate infection of people with deadly or debilitating [[diseases]], exposing people to [[biological weapons|biological]] and [[chemical weapons]], [[human radiation experiments]], injecting people with [[toxic]] and [[radioactive]] chemicals, [[surgical]] experiments, [[interrogation]]/[[torture]] experiments, tests involving [[mind-altering substances]], and a wide variety of others. Many of these tests were performed on [[children]] and [[mentally disabled]] individuals. In many of the studies, a large number of the subjects were [[poverty|poor]], [[racial minorities]], and/or [[Incarceration|prisoners]]. Often, subjects were sick or disabled people, whose doctors told them that they were receiving "medical treatment". They were used as the subjects of harmful and deadly experiments, without their knowledge or consent. In reaction to this, interest groups and institutions have worked to design policies and oversight to ensure that future human subject research in the United States would be ethical and legal.

During World War II, [[Fort Detrick]] in Maryland was the headquarters of US biological warfare experiments. [[Operation Whitecoat]] involved the injection of infectious agents into military forces to observe their effects in human subjects.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/programmes/file_on_4/4701196.stm | work=[[BBC News]] | title=Hidden history of US germ testing | date=2006-02-13 | access-date=2010-05-04 | archive-date=2010-08-23 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100823060943/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/programmes/file_on_4/4701196.stm | url-status=live }}</ref>

Public outcry over the discovery of government experiments on human subjects led to numerous congressional investigations and hearings, including the [[Church Committee]], [[United States President's Commission on CIA activities within the United States|Rockefeller Commission]], and [[Advisory Committee on Human Radiation Experiments]], amongst others. These inquiries have not resulted in prosecutions. Not all subjects involved in the trials have been compensated or notified that they were subjects of such trials.

In the 1950s and 1960s, [[Chester M. Southam]] injected [[HeLa]] cancer cells into healthy individuals, cancer patients, and prison inmates from the [[Ohio Penitentiary]]. This experiment raised many bioethical concerns involving [[informed consent]], [[Primum non nocere|non-maleficence]], and [[Beneficence (ethics)|beneficence]]. Some of Southam's subjects, namely those that already had cancer, were unaware that they were being injected with malignant cells. Additionally, in one of these patients, the cells metastasized to her lymph nodes.<ref name=Skloot>{{cite book|last1=Skloot|first1=Rebecca|title=The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks|date=2010|publisher=Crown/Archetype|location=New York|isbn=9780307589385|pages=127–135}}</ref>

In 1962, the Kefauver-Harris Drug Amendment was passed by the United States Congress. This amendment made changes to the Federal Food Drug & Consumer Act by requiring drug companies to prove both safety and effectiveness of their products. Consequently, drugs were required to have [[Food and Drug Administration]] (FDA) approval before being marketed to consumers. Additionally, informed consent became a participation requirement and rules were put into place. This regulation was influenced by the results of 1950 use of [[thalidomide]] in Western Europe for pregnant women. They were prescribed the [[sedative]] thalidomide, which was inaccurately marketed as a [[morning sickness]] treatment. Women gave birth to more than 12,000 infants born with deformities due to effects from the drug in utero.

In the [[Tuskegee syphilis experiment]] from 1932 to 1972, the United States Public Health Service contracted with the [[Tuskegee Institute]] for a long-term study of syphilis. During the study, more than 600 African-American men were studied who were not told they had syphilis. In an effort to better understand the disease, researchers denied the men access to the known treatment of the antibiotic [[penicillin]]. They recorded observations of the effects of the disease over time. Under the impression they were being treated for "bad blood", the participants were given free healthcare by the government.<ref>Gray, Fred D. ''The Tuskegee Syphilis Study'', Montgomery: New South Books, 1998.</ref> As ineffective treatment was given to the subjects, two-thirds of the group had died by the end of the 40-year experiment. A leak in 1972 led to cessation of the study and severe legal ramifications. It has been widely regarded as the "most infamous biomedical research study in U.S. history".<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Katz RV, Kegeles SS, Kressin NR, etal |title=The Tuskegee Legacy Project: willingness of Minorities to Participate in Biomedical Research |journal=J Health Care Poor Underserved |volume=17 |issue=4 |pages=698–715 |date=November 2006 |pmid=17242525 |pmc=1780164 |doi=10.1353/hpu.2006.0126 }}</ref> Because of the public outrage, in 1974 Congress passed the [[National Research Act]], to provide for protection of human subjects in experiments. The National Commission for the Protection of Human Subjects of Biomedical and Behavioral Research was established. It was tasked with establishing the boundary between research and routine practice, the role of [[risk-benefit analysis]], guidelines for participation, and the definition of informed consent. Its ''[[Belmont Report]]'' established three tenets of ethical research: respect for persons, [[beneficence (ethics)|beneficence]], and justice.<ref>{{citation | url = https://videocast.nih.gov/pdf/ohrp_belmont_report.pdf | author = National Commission for the Protection of Human Subjects of Biomedical and Behavioral Research | date = 1978-09-30 | title = The Belmont Report: Ethical Principles and Guidelines for the Protection of Human Subjects of Research | publisher = [[United States Department of Health, Education and Welfare]] | author-link = National Commission for the Protection of Human Subjects of Biomedical and Behavioral Research | access-date = 2025-07-15 | archive-date = 2019-06-18 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190618212446/https://videocast.nih.gov/pdf/ohrp_belmont_report.pdf | url-status = live }}</ref>

[[Project MKUltra]]—sometimes referred to as the "CIA's mind control program"—was the code name given to an illegal program of experiments on human subjects, designed and undertaken by the United States [[Central Intelligence Agency]] (CIA). Experiments on humans were intended to identify and develop drugs and procedures to be used in interrogations and torture, in order to weaken the individual to force confessions through [[Brainwashing|mind control]]. Organized through the [[Office of Scientific Intelligence|Scientific Intelligence Division]] of the CIA, the project coordinated with the [[U.S. Army Biological Warfare Laboratories|Special Operations Division]] of the U.S. Army's [[Chemical Corps]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www2.gwu.edu/~nsarchiv/radiation/dir/mstreet/commeet/meet4/trnsct04.txt|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130713145805/http://www.gwu.edu/~nsarchiv/radiation/dir/mstreet/commeet/meet4/trnsct04.txt|url-status=dead|title=Advisory on Human Radiation Experiments, July 5, 1994, National Security Archives, retrieved January 16, 2014|archivedate=July 13, 2013}}</ref> The program began in the early 1950s, was officially sanctioned in 1953, was reduced in scope in 1964, further curtailed in 1967 and officially halted in 1973.<ref>{{cite news |title=C.I.A Says It Found More Secret Papers on Behavior Control: Senate Panel Puts Off Hearing to Study Data Dozen Witnesses Said To Have Misled Inquiry C.I.A. Tells Of Finding Secret Data |author=Jo Thomas |newspaper=New York Times |date=3 Sep 1977 }}</ref> The program engaged in many illegal activities;<ref name="nytimes.com"/><ref>[http://www.hss.doe.gov/healthsafety/ohre/roadmap/achre/chap3_4.html Chapter 3: Supreme Court Dissents Invoke the Nuremberg Code: CIA and DOD Human Subjects Research Scandals<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130331150116/http://www.hss.doe.gov/healthsafety/ohre/roadmap/achre/chap3_4.html |date=2013-03-31 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://publicintelligence.net/ssci-mkultra-1977/|title=U.S. Senate Report on CIA MKULTRA Behavioral Modification Program 1977 &#124; Public Intelligence|date=July 27, 2012|website=publicintelligence.net|access-date=July 4, 2015|archive-date=June 15, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180615135505/https://publicintelligence.net/ssci-mkultra-1977/|url-status=live}}</ref> in particular it used unwitting U.S. and Canadian citizens as its test subjects, which led to controversy regarding its legitimacy.<ref name="nytimes.com">{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/packages/pdf/national/13inmate_ProjectMKULTRA.pdf|title=Project MKUltra, the Central Intelligence Agency's Program of Research into Behavioral Modification. Joint Hearing before the Select Committee on Intelligence and the Subcommittee on Health and Scientific Research of the Committee on Human Resources, United States Senate, Ninety-Fifth Congress, First Session|publisher=U.S. Government Printing Office (copy hosted at the New York Times website)|date=August 8, 1977|access-date=2010-04-18|archive-date=2011-04-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110429194235/http://www.nytimes.com/packages/pdf/national/13inmate_ProjectMKULTRA.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>{{rp|page=74}}<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.gwu.edu/~nsarchiv/NSAEBB/NSAEBB54/ | title = Science, Technology and the CIA: A National Security Archive Electronic Briefing Book | editor-last = Richelson | editor-first = JT | access-date = 2009-06-12 | date = 2001-09-10 | publisher = [[George Washington University]] | archive-date = 2015-02-25 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150225171048/http://www2.gwu.edu/~nsarchiv/NSAEBB/NSAEBB54/ | url-status = live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.hss.energy.gov/healthsafety/ohre/roadmap/achre/chap3_4.html | title = Chapter 3, part 4: Supreme Court Dissents Invoke the Nuremberg Code: CIA and DOD Human Subjects Research Scandals | work = Advisory Committee on Human Radiation Experiments Final Report | access-date = 2005-08-24 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070430101158/http://hss.energy.gov/healthsafety/ohre/roadmap/achre/chap3_4.html | archive-date = 2007-04-30 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | publisher = [[United States Congress]] | title = The Select Committee to Study Governmental Operations with Respect to Intelligence Activities, Foreign and Military Intelligence | work = [[Church Committee]] report, no. 94-755, 94th Cong., 2d Sess. | location = [[Washington, D.C.]] | year = 1976 | url = http://www.aarclibrary.org/publib/church/reports/book1/html/ChurchB1_0200b.htm | page = 392 | access-date = 2015-07-04 | archive-date = 2016-03-07 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160307220237/http://www.aarclibrary.org/publib/church/reports/book1/html/ChurchB1_0200b.htm | url-status = live }}</ref> MKUltra used numerous methodologies to manipulate people's mental states and alter brain functions, including the surreptitious administration of drugs (especially [[LSD]]) and other chemicals, [[hypnosis]], assassins| publisher=Skyhorse Publishing| url=https://archive.org/details/ontrailofjfkassa00russ| url-access=registration| quote=MKULTRA hypnosis.| year=2008| page=[https://archive.org/details/ontrailofjfkassa00russ/page/273 273]| isbn=978-1-60239-322-6}}</ref>

===Beecher Paper===
In a 1966 paper, Harvard anesthesiologist [[Henry K. Beecher]] described 22 published medical studies in which patients had been subjects with no expected benefit to the patient of the experiment.<ref name="Beecher1966">{{Cite journal
| last1 = Beecher
| first1 = H. K.
| title = Ethics and Clinical Research
| doi = 10.1056/NEJM196606162742405
| journal = New England Journal of Medicine
| volume = 274
| issue = 24
| pages = 1354–1360
| year = 1966
| pmid = 5327352
| pmc = <!--none-->
| url = https://www.who.int/docstore/bulletin/pdf/2001/issue4/vol79.no.4.365-372.pdf
| archive-date = 2020-01-12
| access-date = 2020-10-05
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200112162701/https://www.who.int/docstore/bulletin/pdf/2001/issue4/vol79.no.4.365-372.pdf
| url-status = live
}} Reprint in Harkness, Lederer & Wikler, 2001, {{PMID|11357216}}</ref> This has been characterized as unethical. For example, patients infused with live cancer cells had been told in one study that they were receiving "some cells", without being told this was cancer. Though identities of the authors and institutions had been stripped, the 22 studies were later identified as having been conducted by mainstream researchers and published in prestigious journals within approximately the previous decade. The 22 cases had been selected from a set of 50 that Beecher had collected. He presented evidence that such unethical studies were widespread and represented a systemic problem in medical research rather than exceptions.<ref name="Beecher1966"/><ref name="Rothman1987">{{Cite journal | last1 = Rothman | first1 = D. J. | title = Ethics and Human Experimentation | doi = 10.1056/NEJM198711053171906 | journal = New England Journal of Medicine | volume = 317 | issue = 19 | pages = 1195–1199 | year = 1987 | pmid = 3309660 | url = http://tracerkinetics.engr.iupui.edu/emorris_web/Ethics%20Course%2009/Journal%20articles/Ethics%20and%20Human%20Experimentation%20Henry%20Beecher%20revisited.pdf | access-date = 2015-09-02 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120206183801/http://tracerkinetics.engr.iupui.edu/emorris_web/Ethics%20Course%2009/Journal%20articles/Ethics%20and%20Human%20Experimentation%20Henry%20Beecher%20revisited.pdf | archive-date = 2012-02-06 }}</ref>

Beecher had been writing about human experimentation and publicizing cases that he considered to be bad practice for nearly a decade. His 1965 briefing to science writers and his 1966 paper gained widespread news coverage and stimulated public reaction.<ref name="Rothman1987"/><ref name="Kopp1999">{{Cite journal
| doi = 10.1097/00000542-199906000-00034
| last1 = Kopp
| first1 = V.
| title = Henry Knowles Beecher and the development of informed consent in anesthesia research
| journal = Anesthesiology
| volume = 90
| issue = 6
| pages = 1756–1765
| year = 1999
| pmid = 10360876
| doi-access = free
}}</ref> The paper has been described as "the most influential single paper ever written about experimentation involving human subjects."<ref name="Harkness2001">{{Cite journal | last1 = Harkness | first1 = J. | last2 = Lederer | first2 = S. | last3 = Wikler | first3 = D. | title = Laying ethical foundations for clinical research | journal = Bulletin of the World Health Organization | volume = 79 | issue = 4 | pages = 365–366 | year = 2001 | pmid = 11357216 | pmc = 2566394}}</ref> The United States [[Office for Human Research Protections]] credits Beecher through this paper as "ultimately contributing to the impetus for the first [[National Institutes of Health|NIH]] and [[Food and Drug Administration|FDA]] regulations."<ref>{{cite web |work=Institutional Review Board Guidebook |title=History of the Human Subjects Protection System |url=https://www.hhs.gov/ohrp/archive/irb/irb_introduction.htm |publisher=[[Office for Human Research Protections]] |year=1993 | access-date = 2011-06-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130218150358/https://www.hhs.gov/ohrp/archive/irb/irb_introduction.htm |archive-date=2013-02-18 }}</ref>

Beecher was instrumental in developing solutions to such abuses. He noted that a common element in these studies was that some experimental subjects, such as military personnel or mentally handicapped children in institutions, were not in a position to freely decline consent.<ref name="Rothman1987"/> Beecher believed that rules requiring informed consent were not alone sufficient, as truly informed consent was an unattainable ideal. He worked both to define the rules and conditions for informed consent, and to establish [[institutional review board]]s as an additional layer of oversight regarding research protocols.<ref name="Rothman1987"/><ref name="Kopp1999"/>

==International drug trials==

Since the late 20th century, African nations have often been the sites of clinical testing by large international pharmaceutical companies. In some cases, rural communities have developed iatrophobia (fear of doctors) after undergoing or learning of highly controversial medical experimentation. The fundamental distrust lies in the potential confrontation of [[Hobson's choice]]: "Experimental medicine or no medicine at all". Multiple cases of ethically questionable experiments have been documented.<ref>Washington, Harriet A. ''[[Medical Apartheid]]'', Anchor Books, 2006, p394</ref>

In the late 20th century, [[Depo-Provera]] was clinically tested on Zimbabwean women. Once approved, the drug was used as a population control measure in the 1970s. Commercial farm owners put pressure on native women workers to accept the use of Depo-Provera.<ref name="Kaler, Amy 1998. p 347">{{cite journal | last1 = Kaler | first1 = Amy | year = 1998 | title = A Threat to the Nation and a Threat to the Men: the Banning of Depo-Provera in Zimbabwe, 1981 | journal = [[Journal of Southern African Studies]] | volume = 24 | issue = 2| page = 347 | doi=10.1080/03057079808708580| bibcode = 1998JSAfS..24..347K }}</ref> Population control interests motivated many of the family planning programs. This led to its eventual ban in Zimbabwe.<ref name="Kaler, Amy 1998. p 347"/>

A 1996 clinical trial in [[Kano (city)|Kano]], Nigeria, <!--when? and how many were treated in the study?--> involving the Pfizer drug [[Trovan]] to treat meningitis resulted in 200 children being disabled and the deaths of 11. Because of these casualties, the [[Abdullahi v. Pfizer, Inc.|Nigerian government sued Pfizer]] over whether it had appropriately obtained informed consent.<ref name="Washington p392-393">Washington, Harriet A. ''[[Medical Apartheid]]'', Anchor Books, 2006, p392-393</ref><ref name="news.bbc.co.uk">{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/africa/6719141.stm |title=Africa &#124; Nigeria sues drugs giant Pfizer |publisher=[[BBC News]] |date=2007-06-05 |access-date=2010-11-12}}</ref> Pfizer argued in court that it had met all regulations for drug testing. Many Nigerians mistrust the use of medical vaccines and also refuse to participate in medical trials.<ref name="Washington p392-393"/>

In 1994 United States drug companies began conducting trials of the drug [[Zidovudine|AZT]] on [[HIV]]-positive African subjects with the goal of developing treatments to reduce the transmission of HIV/AIDS during childbirth.<ref name="ReferenceA">Meier, Benjamin Mason: "International Protection of Persons Undergoing Medical Experimentation: Protecting the Right of Informed Consent", ''[[Berkeley Journal of International Law]]'' [1085-5718] Meier yr:2002 vol:20 iss:3 pg:513 -554</ref> With funding from the [[National Institutes of Health]] (NIH) and [[Centers for Disease Control]] (CDC), the program tested over 17,000 [[Zimbabwean]] women for the efficacy of AZT in preventing transmission of HIV/AIDS during childbirth. Half of the women were given a [[placebo]] rather than the drug, and the subjects were not informed of the potential dangers of the treatment. According to [[Peter Lamptey]], the head of the AIDS Control and Prevention Program, "if you interviewed the people in the study, most wouldn't understand to what they had actually consented."<ref name="ReferenceA"/> An estimated 1000 newborns of women in the study contracted HIV/AIDS, although this could have been avoided by treating the women with known drugs. The testing was ceased in 1998 when the CDC claimed to have obtained sufficient data from experiments in [[Thailand]].<ref name="ReferenceA"/>
